sections.title: Executive verdict
sections.text: Acme Universal Safezone 9 manufactures industrial safety footwear, not railway interiors. Its established factories, certifications and recurring institutional demand are real positives. Growth is modest, returns on expanding capital are weak, and extensive historical restatements do not reconcile cleanly to the final prospectus main statements. The undated input snapshot’s enormous negative cash-flow number is a malformed annual-report comparative, not a verified economic loss. Classification: research hold on financial reliability and current deployment, with a demanding quoted valuation. Conditional BQS 4.28 and Growth Quality 4.00 are not ranking eligible; IAS remains NS. No fraud, conviction or current default is asserted.

sections.title: Research header, identity, scope and gates
sections.text: BSE SME 544964, ACMEUNIV, ISIN INE1KUL01020. Cutoff October 20,2026; nominal INR five-year scenarios,15% equity hurdle before personal taxes. The company converted its predecessor partnership into a company in November 2016 and became public in July 2025. Indian GAAP Accounting Standards under Section 133, not Ind AS; no subsidiary/JV is reported. Final prospectus and official security master support post-IPO 1.909342 crore shares and 1600-share board lot. October 6 listing is corroborated by exchange-notice mirrors, but the underlying BSE PDF was inaccessible; market-maker/group-transition notice is not treated as read primary evidence. G 1 conditional, G 2 hold for material internal financial inconsistencies, G 3 conditional pending post-IPO bridge, G 4 unverified. Historical negative findings can be assessed with Medium confidence while exact corrected profit and current funding have Low confidence.

sections.title: Scorecard and calculation audit
sections.text: Canonical scores: GOV 4, MOAT 5, REV 4, DUR 5, CAP 3, CASH 5, BAL 4, EXEC 4, EARN 3. BQS = .20×4+.20×5+.12×4+.10×5+.12×3+.10×5+.08×4+.08×4 =4.28. GQS = .40×4+.20×5+.15×3+.15×3+.10×5 =4.00. CAP≤3 persistent cap 5 does not bind. Q is 4.28, R is NS, D 2, P 2, L NS; IAS known sum 1.67 with 55% coverage gives raw missing-data interval 2.12–6.17, not a score or reweighted average. All rankings are excluded because G 2 reliability is central. GOV/CASH one-point changes move BQS by.20/.10; EARN/CAP changes move GQS by.15 each. These uncertainties exceed small apparent cross-company score differences.

sections.title: Business overview and unit economics
sections.text: The company manufactures safety shoes and related protective footwear using leather, EVA, nitrile rubber and PVC, across four MP/UP plants and 15 product lines. Reported FY 2026 permanent workforce is 1,073. Direct institutional sales, distributors/dealers and digital channels serve industrial customers. ISO/BIS product qualifications and tooling know-how matter, but raw-material cost, labor, factory utilization and distributor credit drive economics; this is not a subscription business. FY 2026 installed capacity 43.15 lakh pairs versus actual 27.71851 lakh implies 64.23% utilization, versus 63.15% FY 2025 and 77.71% FY 2024. Actual FY 2026 volume grew 6.67%, much less than a high-growth compounder narrative. Proposed machinery improves intermediate bottlenecks and efficiency, not overall installed soling capacity.

sections.title: Moat, industry position and concentration
sections.text: Long operating history, certified protective products, institutional relationships and manufacturing capability support a useful but modest position. Neither recurring replacement demand nor compliance mandates ensure pricing power. FY 2026 largest customer 12.13%, top three 23.01%, top ten 47.71%; exports 8.10%, so overseas expansion is optionality rather than the core engine. FY 2025 top-ten amount₹85.8476 crore divided by sales₹187.3558 crore is 45.82%, whereas the printed percentage says 48.82%; use the amount-based calculation and flag the discrepancy. Top-ten suppliers 52.88% of purchases and largest 15.92% expose material sourcing dependence. Long-term rate contracts/annual institutional agreements are described, but minimum committed volumes and a quantified binding order book were not established. Mallcom, Liberty Shoes and Superhouse are operational reference points with different product/export mixes; issuer-selected peer working-capital tables are not independently verified peer valuations.

sections.title: Revenue growth and scale
sections.text: Restated revenue FY 2023–2026 is₹157.7096/178.9440/187.3558/205.9032 crore. Comparable three-year CAGR 9.30% maps to REV 4; FY 2025 grew 4.70% and FY 2026 9.90%. Revenue recognition was itself corrected during restatement, so exact growth confidence is Medium rather than High. Do not use the IPO price jump, capacity nameplate or export-market TAM as operating growth. FY 2026 domestic sales₹189.1082, exports₹16.6699 and SEZ₹.1251 reconcile to total. No original FY 2022 series was established, and no synthetic five-year history is manufactured.

sections.title: Growth quality and reinvestment runway
sections.text: Capital was invested well ahead of realized profits: PPE plus CWIP increased from₹48.7635 crore FY 2024 to₹59.7797 FY 2025 and₹62.7834 FY 2026. FY 2024–2026 cash capex₹15.3741/18.8094/12.6477 totals₹46.8312 crore. Equity+debt−free-cash invested-capital proxy rises₹86.4215→96.3052→109.9200; pledged FDs remain employed capital. Normalized operating EBIT retaining procurement discounts/export incentives but removing specified noncore income and actuarial gains is approximately₹12.4513/5.5161/9.0695. At 25% tax, two-year incremental NOPAT is negative despite₹23.4985 additional capital; FY 2026 recovery alone implies about 19.57% incremental return, a genuine positive but not proof of durable excess returns. Average-capital FY 2026 normalized return is roughly 6.6%, below an analyst 12–16% capital-cost range. CAP 3 reflects the full period, not a claim every new machine destroys value.

sections.title: Management, governance and execution
sections.text: Promoters Nitin and Ruchi Tiwari hold a projected post-issue 69.74% based on final capital tables. Their FY 2026 remuneration₹2.52 crore plus rent₹.972 crore is substantial against reported PAT₹5.8575 crore; disclosed contracts do not independently establish arm’s-length pricing. Director loans₹13.3906 crore are interest-free but repayable on demand, a funding benefit with withdrawal risk, not loans diverted to promoters. Prior auditor Solanki Singh & Co resigned September 1,2025 citing unavoidable circumstances; Ramanand & Associates was appointed September 25. This is not described as normal rotation or a proven dispute. Signed FY 2026 audit opinion/IFC are unmodified; auditor reports audit trails operating and no actual borrowing default. Contrary evidence is the breadth of restatement corrections and the final reconciliation failures. No blanket clean-governance inference is made. Capacity commissioning and higher output demonstrate execution, but lower utilization and weak capital returns limit the score.

sections.title: Financial forensics, cash conversion and legal matters
sections.text: Main restated PAT FY 2023–2026 is₹3.0062/7.5647/.8044/5.8575 crore. The final reconciliation instead ends FY 2025 at₹1.7329 and FY 2026 at₹5.2410; reserves reconciliation also differs from the main balance sheet. Original FY 2026 annual PAT is a₹5.4696 crore loss after₹11.2143 crore prior-period expense, whereas the prospectus reconciliation starts from a different₹6.0921 crore loss. Adjustments include employee benefits, deferred tax, GST, unrecorded liabilities, revenue cutoff, inventory, grants and depreciation. These are material reporting questions, not grounds to choose whichever PAT looks best. Main CFO FY 2023–2026 is₹.5322/10.8772/12.5322/7.5178; the FY 2025 original comparative contains a wildly mis-scaled CFO/FD offset, explaining the snapshot anomaly. FY 2024–2026 CFO₹30.9272 is 217.4% of main PAT₹14.2266 before financing-classified cash interest₹8.8742; after interest₹22.0530 is 155.0%, but less than₹46.8312 capex. High depreciation helps cash conversion; positive CFO is not free cash flow. FY 2026 CFO absorbed inventory₹3.9663, other current assets₹4.1428 and payable reduction₹1.5699. Detailed payable notes and balance-sheet components are₹22.9960 in 2026 versus₹24.5660 in 2025, consistent with CFO; reversing these columns would invent a discrepancy. AR₹28.7985 has only₹.1097 over one year and no allowance; inventory₹35.2325, supplier advances₹1.8713 and AP₹22.9960 give actual core WC₹42.9063. Other current assets₹11.3337 include₹10.4235 government balances, not free cash. The MSME disclosure separately reports₹22.5150 principal versus₹11.2575 in the payable note, another unresolved inconsistency. Three GST disputes total about₹.84935 crore; four trademark oppositions remain pending, including one without a filed counterstatement at disclosure. Allegations are not findings. Detailed bank guarantees₹.4852 crore are not automatically incremental debt.

sections.title: Valuation, normalized earnings and linked scenarios
sections.text: Secondary October 19 last trade₹119.90 times 1.909342 crore shares gives₹228.9301 crore market value. Main PAT implies 39.08 x earnings, not pre-IPO weighted EPS. Bounded normalization starts from main PBT₹7.8164, removes₹.9189 bank interest/asset profit/grant/miscellaneous income and₹1.0112 actuarial gain, retains operating discounts/drawback/RODTEP, and applies 25–30% tax: PAT₹4.1204–4.4147 crore. Excluding FX gain too gives₹3.8991–4.1776. Thus roughly 52–59 x bounded earnings, not a verified corrected profit. The model starts with actual₹42.9063 core WC,₹.8941 free cash and₹58.0459 debt, adds₹31.2142 net IPO once, excludes₹2.3704 pledged FD, charges₹12.5802 machinery/solar plus 18% tax cash sensitivity, and charges₹10.634 unidentified acquisition/GCP with no invented profit contribution. Incremental WC is 30% of positive sales additions; maintenance capex starts₹8 crore and debt amortization₹3.8073 then₹3.5 annually. Base growth 8/8/7/6/5%,5% EBIT margin and 7 x EBITDA produces₹74.27 terminal price and−9.13% annual return, funded under assumptions. Bull 15/15/12/10/8%,7% margin and 9 x gives₹161.96 and 6.20%, still below 15% hurdle. A margin 4–6% by multiple 5–9 x grid and 12/15/18% hurdle entry sensitivities are retained in the model. Base hurdle-compatible prices₹42.15/36.93/32.47 are conditional, not observable fair value. R remains NS because the unresolved earnings reconciliation and current deployment materially affect a point return.

sections.title: Bear case, balance sheet and permanent-loss path
sections.text: March debt₹58.0459 includes₹13.3906 interest-free promoter loans and bank/current maturities; free cash is only₹.8941. Cash-credit limit₹30 crore versus₹27.0102 drawn offers limited headroom, not guaranteed rescue. IPO capital improves resilience but actual deployment/October borrowings were not verified. Bear sales−20%, then 0/3/3/3%,2% EBIT margin,11% bank borrowing cost,45 extra collection days,15% inventory loss,10% debtor loss,20% other-current-asset loss, GST payout and full promoter demand repayment generate₹54.12 crore funding gap. No rescue/dilution is invented; terminal equity under that unfunded arithmetic is zero, not a forecast or probability. Permanent impairment can arise from weak returns, trapped tax balances, refinancing stress and dilution at unfavorable prices even without fraud. Risk is High. Downside resilience D 2 reflects verified liabilities and explicit stresses with Medium input confidence, not an observed default.

sections.title: Five-times and ten-times feasibility
sections.text: At constant shares,5 x/10 x prices require₹1,144.65/2,289.30 crore equity value. At an illustrative 20 x earnings multiple, that means₹57.23/114.47 crore sustainable PAT, roughly 13–15 x/26–29 x the bounded current earnings base. Over five years this requires extraordinary earnings compounding, far beyond observed 9.30% revenue CAGR and constrained by 64% utilization, reinvestment and working capital. Margin recovery can help, but no capacity, signed demand or return evidence presently supports such targets. This is feasibility arithmetic, not a prediction or claimed impossibility.

sections.title: Monitoring, ownership and tradability
sections.text: Priority checks are a signed reconciliation connecting original FY 2026 loss, restatement schedule and main profit/equity; correction of MSME and comparative CFO tables; actual IPO deployment and tax-inclusive project costs; subsequent GST-balance receipts; debtor ageing and supplier settlement; borrowing/amortization and promoter-loan terms; utilization and incremental returns after machinery; GST/trademark outcomes. Official master confirms 1600 shares per lot, costing₹191,840 at the dated secondary quote. A₹5 lakh position is about 2.6 lots, so lot granularity matters. Only about ten listed sessions existed by October 19; no pre-listing day is treated as zero volume. Multiple master-series rows have different bands, and the announced transition after cutoff cannot prove the active regime at cutoff. Complete BSE post-listing turnover, restrictions and live depth were not independently established. L and practical exit-days remain NS. Recovered dated secondary history corroborates the October 19 quote and contains 9 post-listing rows, fewer than a complete 20/60-session series. Observed lower-turnover median is ₹6992000 per day, giving a purely illustrative ₹5 lakh / 5% participation exit of 1.43 observed sessions. Low/high times volume are turnover bounds, not reported turnover. The short IPO record, missing listing-session row and unverified BSE restrictions keep L NS; pre-listing dates remain excluded.

sections.title: Final classification and conditional action
sections.text: Completed deep assessment with a financial-reliability hold, not a pending screen and not an actionable purchase recommendation. BQS 4.28 and GQS 4.00 are explicitly conditional analytical judgments and excluded from numerical ranking. Strongest positive counterargument is established manufacturing plus positive main-statement operating cash generation and fresh equity. Strongest negative evidence is weak capital productivity, expensive bounded earnings and unclosed accounting reconciliations. A clean post-IPO cash/debt bridge and internally consistent audited numbers are prerequisites to revisit IAS; an unexplained new related-party use or overdue financing would worsen the classification. The old archive and original input values are preserved, with corrections stated rather than silently overwritten.

sections.title: Sources, assumptions and unresolved evidence
sections.text: Sources are linked below and tied to sections. Final prospectus main statements control tabulated history, while conflicting reconciliations remain explicitly visible; this is not a claim they have been corrected. Earlier FY 2023 comes from the March DRHP, not an invented extension. Primary PDFs were downloaded and read locally when the web parser failed. Quote is a dated secondary last trade, not an exchange-certified close; the official master corroborates identity/capital/lot only. No independent current peer prices, credit-rating outcome, full BSE surveillance clearance, post-IPO deployment report or signed reconciliation was established. Scenario margins, tax, capital needs, multiple and stresses are analyst assumptions; no acquisition earnings, new debt or dividends are manufactured. Financial-history corrections and all low-confidence gaps remain part of the completed dossier.
